en: And in fact, their export capacity, their production capacity in China is so large, it could basically take care of the entire North America market.

en: Their average Chinese vehicle has four to $5,000 of subsidies indirect and direct from the government.

en: Yeah, because I was going to ask, is that what keeps the price down the scale of the manufacturing they're doing or how much of it is sort of the subsidies that they're getting?

en: Both.

zh: 两者都是。

zh: 西方公司在中国赚了很多钱，赚了很长时间，福特没有，但我们的许多竞争对手赚了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They made just billions and billions.
zh: 他们赚了数十亿又数十亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the Chinese government are very practical.
zh: 而且我认为中国政府非常务实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, just like solar and others, we want to really dominate global automotive.
zh: 嘿，就像太阳能和其他领域一样，我们要真正主导全球汽车业。

en: So we're going to bet on this change of
zh: 所以我们要押注这个变革——

en: Propulsion, electrification.

speaker: Unknown
en: And they made this bet many years ago.
zh: 而且他们很多年前就下了这个注。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing about cars that everyone knows, but when you point it out, they're like, oh yeah, I guess that makes sense.
zh: 关于汽车有一点人人都知道，但当你指出来时，他们会说，哦对，我想这说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: These cars have 10 cameras in them.
zh: 这些车里有 10 个摄像头。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have sophisticated communication.
zh: 它们有复杂的通信系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're all connected.
zh: 它们全部联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're autonomous in many ways.
zh: 它们在很多方面是自动驾驶的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these vehicles should be reviewed by the Defense Department for national security.
zh: 所以这些车辆应该由国防部进行国家安全审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have sensitive PI information.
zh: 它们有敏感的个人身份信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have camera images of your whole life, where you drive, including a military base, an electrical substation, all sorts of stuff.
zh: 它们有你整个人生的摄像头影像，你开车去哪里，包括军事基地、变电站，各种各样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were personally driving a Chinese EV, which someone could see as like, oh, that's kind of a diss to Ford branded vehicles.
zh: 你本人开一辆中国电动车，有人可能会觉得，哦，这有点像是打福特品牌车的脸。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it seems like maybe that was the point to sort of motivate everybody to say like, you got to get in this game.
zh: 但看起来也许这就是目的所在，去激励所有人说，你必须加入这场比赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Xiaomi, yes.
zh: 小米，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: SU7.
zh: SU7。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why, why, why?
zh: 为什么，为什么，为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're an American and you want us to beat the Chinese in the car business, you're all going to want to pay attention, not necessarily to Tesla.
zh: 如果你是一个美国人，你希望我们在汽车生意上打败中国人，你们都会想密切关注，不一定是 Tesla。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing against Tesla.
zh: 不是针对 Tesla。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've been doing great, but, you know, they really don't have an updated vehicle.
zh: 他们一直做得很好，但是，你知道，他们真的没有一款更新的车型。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best in business for us, cost-wise and competition-wise, supply chain, manufacturing expertise, the IP in the vehicle was really BYD.
zh: 对我们来说，在成本上、竞争上、供应链上、制造专业能力上、车辆的知识产权上，业界最好的真的是 BYD。

speaker: Unknown
en: And BYD became the most volume brand in China, not VW or the Western brands last year.
zh: 而且 BYD 去年成为中国销量最大的品牌，不是 VW 或西方品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Geely actually just surpassed it now.
zh: 实际上吉利现在刚刚超越了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we're smart, we'll take the cost competitiveness of BYD and then we'll compete with that platform in parts of the market where we know our customers really well.
zh: 如果我们聪明，我们会拿 BYD 的成本竞争力，然后在我们非常了解客户的部分市场用那个平台去竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this kind of next cycle of EV customers in the US, they want pickups and utilities and all these different body styles, but they want it at $30,000, not $50,000, like the first inning.
zh: 而美国的下一轮电动车客户，他们想要皮卡、多功能车和各种不同的车身形式，但他们想要 3 万美元的价格，而不是像第一局那样的 5 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want it affordably.
zh: 他们想要买得起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, that is the gift that China gave us, to be fearful and respectful enough of their progress that we could not organically just phone it in.
zh: 是的，这就是中国给我们的礼物，让我们对他们的进步足够恐惧和敬畏，以至于我们无法只是敷衍了事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We needed to do what Americans do great sometimes, which is use innovation to compete against the best in the world.
zh: 我们需要做美国人有时最擅长的事，那就是用创新去与世界最强者竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just, for the listeners here who may not know, can you just make sure that you explain what the UEV project is, the universal EV project?
zh: 你能不能，为这里的听众，他们可能不知道，你能不能解释一下 UEV 项目是什么，通用电动车项目？

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: The UEV is kind of like the Model T of the modern Ford.
zh: UEV 有点像现代福特的 Model T。

speaker: Unknown
en: When Henry invented the Model T, you know, my grandfather worked on the line then, he brought a lot of innovation.
zh: 当 Henry 发明 Model T 的时候，你知道，我祖父当时就在那条生产线上工作，他带来了很多创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: He brought the moving assembly line.
zh: 他带来了移动装配线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cars were not made that way.
zh: 汽车以前不是那样制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He got the best materials, but he applied it to the most affordable vehicle.
zh: 他拿到了最好的材料，但把它应用到了最实惠的车上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Universal electric vehicle platform was developed not by Ford, but by a Skunk Works team out in California, mostly motorsports and Tesla folks that we had hired.
zh: 通用电动车平台不是由福特开发的，而是由加州的一支臭鼬工厂团队开发的，主要是我们雇来的赛车运动和 Tesla 背景的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said to the team,
zh: 我们对团队说，

speaker: Unknown
en: You could do anything.
zh: 你们可以随心所欲。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just want you to engineer the most affordable, most efficient electric vehicle on the planet better than BYD.
zh: 我们只希望你们打造出地球上最实惠、最高效的电动车，要比 BYD 更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they got to work.
zh: 然后他们就开工了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't use the Ford system to develop the vehicle and the platform.
zh: 他们没有用福特的体系来开发这辆车和这个平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out that that wound up being a really good bet.
zh: 而事实证明，这是一个非常好的赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: The UAV is three parts.
zh: UAV 由三部分组成。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a large unit casting in the front and the rear.
zh: 前部和后部各有一个大型一体式压铸件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the center is a battery.
zh: 中间则是电池。

speaker: Unknown
en: So radical simplification of vehicle, about 30% less parts.
zh: 这是车辆的彻底简化，零部件减少了大约 30%。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't build the car all in one sequence like we have for 125 years.
zh: 我们不再像过去 125 年那样按单一顺序制造整辆车。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually build the front of the car, separately from the rear of the car, separately from the middle of the car.
zh: 我们实际上是分开制造车的前部、车的后部、车的中部。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the end, we join them together.
zh: 最后再把它们接合在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've never built a car like that.
zh: 我们从来没有这样造过车。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to get the cost down for our customers, we need to radically shrink the size of the battery.
zh: 而为了给客户降低成本，我们需要大幅缩小电池的尺寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: We couldn't BYD on the cost.
zh: 我们没法在成本上赢 BYD。

speaker: Unknown
en: We might as well out-innovate them on efficiency.
zh: 那我们不妨在效率上用创新超越他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we radically engineered the vehicle for efficiency.
zh: 于是我们围绕效率对这辆车进行了彻底的工程设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are just some of the examples.
zh: 这些只是一些例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: People will learn more.
zh: 人们会了解到更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vehicle comes out next year.
zh: 这款车明年发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll show it probably late this year.
zh: 我们可能会在今年晚些时候展示它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited.
zh: 我真的很兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a platform.
zh: 这是一个平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just one vehicle.
zh: 它不只是一辆车。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there'll be multiple vehicles off this platform.
zh: 所以这个平台将会衍生出多款车型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's kind of a Model T moment for us.
zh: 这对我们来说有点像 Model T 的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've always been known for your candor.
zh: 大家一直都知道你敢于直言。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've talked about sort of no more boring products, which implies at least some of Ford's products are boring, which it doesn't necessarily have to do with the technology of it, right?
zh: 你说过“不要再有无聊的产品”，这至少暗示福特的部分产品是无聊的，而这不一定和它的技术有关，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it has more to do with, I don't know, the design, the passion?
zh: 也许它更多与……我不知道，设计、热情有关？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say I believe that Ford
zh: 我想说，我相信福特

speaker: Unknown
en: is best naturally working on, I would call vehicles with deep passion.
zh: 天然最擅长的，是我称之为充满深度热情的车辆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Work, off-road, on-road, passion vehicles.
zh: 工作、越野、公路，这些带有热情属性的车辆。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have the Mustang GTD right behind me.
zh: 我身后就有一辆 Mustang GTD。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mustang is a passion vehicle.
zh: Mustang 就是一辆有热情属性的车。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think a two-row crossover, it's kinda like, I say Wolfgang Puck, he said, you know, there are a lot of really nice restaurants, but it's hard to do a buffet in Vegas.
zh: 但我觉得两排座跨界车，就有点像——我引用 Wolfgang Puck 的话，他说过，你知道，有很多非常好的餐厅，但在拉斯维加斯做自助餐很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if you wanna do a two-row crossover in our industry, RAV4, CRV, whatever, you can make it that, or you can make it a Bronco Sport.
zh: 你知道，如果你想在我们的行业里做一辆两排座跨界车，RAV4、CRV 之类的，你可以把它做成那样，或者可以做成 Bronco Sport。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Bronco Sport fits our brand.
zh: 我认为 Bronco Sport 符合我们的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think Escape, the past Escape did.
zh: 我不认为 Escape，过去的 Escape 符合。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that it needs to be fancy or expensive or has to be super, you know, performance oriented.
zh: 这不是说它必须华丽、昂贵，或者必须是超级，你知道，以性能为导向的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't mean no boring products that way.
zh: 我说“不要再有无聊的产品”不是那个意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think, you know, some of our products were not differentiating.
zh: 我只是觉得，你知道，我们的一些产品没有形成差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we don't want to phone it in.
zh: 所以我们不想敷衍了事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want vehicles at Ford that are truly differentiating for their customers.
zh: 我们希望福特的车对它们的客户而言是真正有差异化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if not, stop making them.
zh: 如果做不到，就停产。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, which is hard to make that call sometimes when there are stakeholders who are bought into that, but sometimes you gotta move away.
zh: 我的意思是，有时候做这个决定很难，因为有利益相关者已经投入其中了，但有时候你必须放弃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially when you compete in the middle of the market and you don't have a cost advantage.
zh: 尤其是当你在市场中段竞争而你又没有成本优势的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really believe Ford is about to launch a number of affordable vehicles, not just the UEV platform, but a number of them.
zh: 我真的相信福特即将推出一系列实惠的车型，不只是 UEV 平台，而是许多款。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll see that come out in the next couple of years.
zh: 你会看到这一点在未来几年显现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I wish we could have done affordable vehicles or sedans.
zh: 唉，真希望我们早就能做经济型车或者轿车。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 很久以前，但我们决定不在美国推出轿车，因为在我们的公司认真对待成本和质量之前，我们没有有竞争力的成本基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really didn't have the rights to compete.
zh: 我们真的没有竞争的资格。

zh: 如果我知道每辆车 Compared to Corolla 或 Civic 要亏 4000 美元，我就没法把资本分配给 Fusion 或 Focus。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to transform my costs, go back to the mountain.
zh: 我需要转变我的成本，回到山上去。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, figure out how we get radically get the cost out of the platforms and then we can compete.
zh: 你知道，想办法从根本上把平台成本降下来，然后我们才能竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we do compete in those, I would say ubiquitous segments, we better bring something new to the table.
zh: 而如果我们要在这些无处不在的细分市场竞争，我们最好拿出一些新东西来。

en: Jim's urgency is pretty intense, but as he explains, it's a competitive market with a lot at stake.

zh: 让我们回到对话中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned Ford as a brand a couple of times.
zh: 你有几次提到 Ford 这个品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Ford is a quintessential American brand, which can seem like a double-edged sword right now.
zh: 我是说，Ford 是一个典型的美国品牌，这现在看起来可能像一把双刃剑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, domestically, the country feels divided.
zh: 我是说，在国内，这个国家感觉是分裂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything gets politicized, even Super Bowl halftime show.
zh: 一切都被政治化，连超级碗中场秀都不例外。

speaker: Unknown
en: Internationally, the U.S. isn't...
zh: 在国际上，美国不再……

speaker: Unknown
en: As embraced as it once was.
zh: 像从前那样受到欢迎了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just curious how those realities come into your calculations.
zh: 我只是好奇这些现实是如何进入你的考量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see people in America wanting authentic companies who are who they are and they have principles.
zh: 我们看到美国人想要真实的公司，它们表里如一，有自己的原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Ford is a principle company.
zh: 而 Ford 是一家有原则的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a reason why we dominate the work sector.
zh: 我们主导工作车领域是有原因的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're 45% of the work vehicles sold in the United States.
zh: 在美国销售的工作车辆中，我们占 45%。

speaker: Unknown
en: We earned our American credentials.
zh: 我们赢得了我们的美国资质。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did not go bankrupt in 2008.
zh: 我们在 2008 年没有破产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our employees did not let the company go bankrupt.
zh: 我们的员工没有让公司破产。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of Americans do care about that.
zh: 很多美国人确实在乎这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't make one F-150 outside the US.
zh: 我们没有在美国境外生产哪怕一辆 F-150。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our competitors all do.
zh: 我们的竞争对手全都在境外生产。

speaker: Unknown
en: They make it in Mexico and Canada.
zh: 他们在墨西哥和加拿大生产。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can't tell, they don't want you to find it.
zh: 而且你看不出来,他们不想让你发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you go into that windshield and you look at that VIN number and you go do a search, you'll find out.
zh: 但你去看那个挡风玻璃,查一下那个 VIN 号码,搜索一下,你就会发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we're proud of our American credentials.
zh: 所以我认为我们对自己的美国资质感到自豪。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when people think of Ford, there may be a $300,000 GTD, but they know that it's the same company that makes the white F-150 for their electrician or the cop car or, you know, the first responder vehicle.
zh: 所以当人们想到 Ford 时,可能有一辆 30 万美元的 GTD,但他们知道这是同一家公司,为他们的电工生产白色 F-150,或者警车,或者你知道的,急救人员用车。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a positive because they don't associate our Americanness with politics.
zh: 而这是积极的,因为他们不把我们的美国属性和政治联系在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: They associate it with jobs.
zh: 他们把它和工作岗位联系在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our understanding of how Americans use vehicles.
zh: 还有我们对美国人如何使用车辆的理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ford is back in Formula One after 22 year absence, partnering with Team Red Bull.
zh: Ford 在缺席 22 年后重返一级方程式,与 Red Bull 车队合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious why now, like, because, I mean, there's F1's cultural growth, there's its new lead into hybrid engines and sustainable fuels.
zh: 我很好奇为什么是现在,因为,我是说,F1 有文化上的增长,还有它新近转向混合动力发动机和可持续燃料。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what's the motivation?
zh: 比如,动机是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: We got into it for a couple of reasons.
zh: 我们参与进来有几个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one, that the rules were changing.
zh: 第一,规则在改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were going to 50% electric, as you said, with sustainable fuel.
zh: 正如你所说,他们将走向 50% 电动,并使用可持续燃料。

speaker: Unknown
en: We like that.
zh: 我们喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also a sport that's really captured the imagination of Americans, like football and other sports.
zh: 这也是一项真正抓住了美国人想象力的运动,就像橄榄球和其他运动一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an indigenous sport to our company.
zh: 这是我们公司土生土长的运动。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we don't make shampoo, we make cars.
zh: 你知道,我们不做洗发水,我们造车。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cars get raced, and the ultimate racing is Formula One.
zh: 汽车会被用来比赛,而终极的赛车就是一级方程式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we like that, but we really like the tech transfer.
zh: 所以我们喜欢这一点,但我们真正喜欢的是技术转移。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is predictive failure components, which we can apply to our work vehicles.
zh: 它是预测性故障部件,我们可以应用到我们的工作车辆上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have almost a million subscriptions now at Ford.
zh: 我们在 Ford 现在有近 100 万份订阅。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of it is productivity software.
zh: 大部分是生产力软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Predictive failure is definitely the next wave of our commercial software productivity.
zh: 预测性故障绝对是我们商用软件生产力的下一波浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want customers to know when something's going to fail on their Ford and Formula One's really good at that.
zh: 我们想让客户知道他们的 Ford 上什么东西快要坏了,而一级方程式在这方面非常擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to do that.
zh: 他们必须做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look at our UEV team.
zh: 看看我们的 UEV 团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would not have the talent in our UEV team if we didn't have, you know, a connection with Formula One.
zh: 如果我们与一级方程式没有联系,我们的 UEV 团队就不会拥有这样的人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you've said some bracing things about the U.S. workforce overall, that America's sort of sleepwalking into a crisis for essential blue-collar workers and that AI will hammer white-collar workers.
zh: 我知道你对美国整体劳动力说过一些令人警醒的话,说美国正在梦游般地走向一场危机,对于基本蓝领工人而言,而 AI 将重创白领工人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's sort of this double whammy.
zh: 这有点像双重打击。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm curious where you are on that right now and what you feel like can be done or should be done, whether that's in Washington, in Silicon Valley, in corporate America overall.
zh: 我很好奇你现在对这件事的看法,以及你觉得能做什么或应该做什么,无论是在华盛顿、硅谷,还是整个美国企业界。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call this sector of jobs the essential economy.
zh: 我们把这个就业领域称为基本经济。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about it, the electricians, the plumbers, the truck drivers, the emergency workers, the construction workers, all the people in our country that make our country run.
zh: 想想看,电工、水管工、卡车司机、急救人员、建筑工人,所有让我们的国家运转的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But our competitors all sent work overseas, so there was not as much need in our education system for trade schools, apprenticeships, you know, all these things that our grandparents and parents used to do.
zh: 但我们的竞争对手都把工作外包到海外,所以我们的教育体系里对职业学校、学徒制,你知道的,我们的祖辈和父辈曾经做的这些事情,就没有那么大的需求了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all those jobs got shipped overseas.
zh: 所有那些工作都被外包到了海外。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, now, oh, we have to build data centers.
zh: 那么,现在,哦,我们得建数据中心了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we need emergency workers.
zh: 现在我们需要急救人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need plumbers and electricians, especially welders for all these AI data centers.
zh: 我们需要水管工和电工,尤其是为所有这些 AI 数据中心服务的焊工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Ford sees us through our customers because we're 45% share of the commercial market in the US.
zh: Ford 通过我们的客户看到了这一点,因为我们在美国商用车市场占有 45% 的份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are our customers.
zh: 这些就是我们的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: They buy our vehicles and they all say the same thing to us.
zh: 他们购买我们的车辆,他们对我们说的话都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ford, can you help me find the next generation of my team?
zh: Ford,你能帮我找到我团队的下一代吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: My average electrician's 57 years old.
zh: 我的电工平均年龄 57 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're gonna be retiring soon.
zh: 他们很快就要退休了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we decided to get serious about this.
zh: 所以我们决定认真对待这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a conference in Detroit last fall, and we started to find like-minded companies with similar issues.
zh: 去年秋天我们在底特律办了一次会议，我们开始寻找有类似问题的志同道合的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're now talking to them.
zh: 我们现在正在和它们谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're allocating serious resources to this.
zh: 我们正在为此投入大量资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're talking to the Ad Council for starting to build awareness of how great these jobs are.
zh: 我们正在和 Ad Council 谈，开始建立人们对这些工作有多好的认知。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, my son can graduate from high school, can be a technician in a Ford dealership and make 150 grand in three years.
zh: 你知道，我的儿子可以从高中毕业，可以在一家 Ford 经销店当技师，三年赚 15 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's not going to get that opportunity if he goes to a four-year degree.
zh: 如果他去读四年制学位，他就得不到那样的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we need to build awareness that these are good jobs, that you can have a great life.
zh: 所以我们需要建立认知：这些是好工作，你可以过上很好的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also need to build more infrastructure in our country, trade schools, apprentice programs.
zh: 我们还需要在我们的国家建设更多基础设施、贸易学校、学徒项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need help from the government.
zh: 我们需要政府的帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also can't rely on the government.
zh: 我们也不能依赖政府。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to do it ourselves.
zh: 我们必须自己动手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your choices about what you're passionate about, your leadership, it has an echo effect beyond Ford's business itself, right?
zh: 你关于自己热爱什么的选择、你的领导力，会在 Ford 业务本身之外产生回响效应，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how much do you think about that responsibility beyond your own shareholders?
zh: 对于超出你自己股东范围的那份责任，你有多少考虑？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I say I have no rights to play any role outside of being the CEO of Ford and making the company successful without progress at Ford.
zh: 嗯，我说，除了作为 Ford 的 CEO、让公司成功，如果没有 Ford 的进步，我无权扮演任何其他角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the most important thing.
zh: 这是最重要的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need to continue to make breakthroughs in quality and cost and electrifications.
zh: 我们需要继续在质量、成本和电气化方面取得突破。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to be profitable.
zh: 我们需要盈利。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to build a sustainable company, but I work for the Ford family.
zh: 我们需要打造一家可持续的公司，但我是为 Ford 家族工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not a family that is interested in the car business because it's an interesting business, so they've been in it for six generations.
zh: 这个家族对汽车业务感兴趣，并不是因为这是个有趣的行业——他们已经干这个六代人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are all completely committed to the industrial future of our country.
zh: 他们所有人都完全致力于我们国家的工业未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, I want our country to succeed long-term against China and others.
zh: 是的，我希望我们的国家长期在与中国及其他国家的竞争中成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that Ford is the kind of company that actually requires a leader like that.
zh: 而且我认为 Ford 正是那种确实需要这样一位领导者的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's at stake for Ford right now?
zh: Ford 现在面临什么利害攸关的事？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's at stake at Ford and our story of success is pretty simple.
zh: 我认为 Ford 面临的利害攸关和我们成功的故事其实很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really reflects the future of our country, not because we are a country, but because Ford is the heart and soul of our industrial base in our country.
zh: 我认为它真的反映了我们国家的未来，不是因为我们是一个国家，而是因为 Ford 是我们国家工业基础的心脏和灵魂。

speaker: Unknown
en: We won't be able to defend ourselves.
zh: 我们将无法自卫。

speaker: Unknown
en: We won't have jobs for the future generations.
zh: 我们将没有面向未来世代的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We won't be able to reduce CO2 at large scale without Ford being able to do that, impact our communities positively, not just with economic benefits, but with social progress.
zh: 如果 Ford 做不到大规模减排 CO2，我们就无法大规模减少 CO2，无法积极地影响我们的社区——不仅仅是经济利益，还有社会进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the kind of scale that Ford has, the kind of impact we have on our country, the importance of our sustainment is really tied to the success of the country and even the defense of the country.
zh: 这就是 Ford 拥有的那种规模，我们对国家的那种影响，我们持续存在的重要性真的与国家的成功甚至国家的防卫紧密相连。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what's at stake.
zh: 这就是利害攸关的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds like a lot of pressure, the way you describe it there.
zh: 听起来压力很大，按你这样描述的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, do you sleep at night, you know, or worry about it?
zh: 就是说，你晚上睡得着吗，你知道的，还是会为此担忧？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, I don't think so.
zh: 不，不，我不觉得会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a problem solver.
zh: 我是一个解决问题的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I literally love problem solving.
zh: 我真的热爱解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yeah, of course, anyone in my position loses sleep, especially when we do the stuff we don't wanna do, like layoffs and restructuring.
zh: 所以，是的，当然，处在我这个位置的人都会失眠，尤其是当我们做那些不想做的事情时，比如裁员和重组。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the worst part of my job.
zh: 这是我工作中最糟糕的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But sometimes you have to shrink to grow like we have at Ford.
zh: 但有时候你必须先收缩才能增长，就像我们在 Ford 做的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And almost six years of leadership in the position, I feel like we're in a good spot.
zh: 在这个职位上快六年了，我觉得我们处在一个不错的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're making progress and we really can change our country and make our country stronger and do everything we need to do with shareholders.
zh: 我们正在取得进展，我们真的能改变我们的国家、让我们的国家更强大，并做好我们对股东需要做的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really believe that in my heart or else I'm not the right leader for Ford.
zh: 我发自内心地相信这一点，否则我就不是 Ford 合适的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Jim, this was great.
zh: 好的，Jim，这次对话非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much for doing it.
zh: 非常感谢你来参加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the best to you, Bob, and appreciate the time.
zh: 祝你一切顺利，Bob，感谢你抽出时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me on.
zh: 谢谢你们邀请我来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jim has always been passionate, and as Ford's CEO, that urgency is definitely front and center.
zh: Jim 一直充满激情，而作为 Ford 的 CEO，那种紧迫感绝对是摆在最前面的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm struck by his sense of responsibility that Ford's mission goes beyond mobility to positively impacting community and country.
zh: 让我印象深刻的是他的责任感：Ford 的使命超越了出行本身，延伸到积极地影响社区和国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, one could look at that cynically, that he's wrapping Ford in the American flag to help differentiate it.
zh: 当然，人们可以带着怀疑的眼光看待这一点，认为他是在用美国国旗包裹 Ford 以帮助实现差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's a bigger picture sensibility at play too, a holistic view of long-term impacts that many business leaders would prefer to brush aside.
zh: 但还有一个更宏观层面的考量在起作用，一种对长期影响的整体视角，而许多商业领袖宁愿对此避而不谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's courage in that, even if it also helps the brand.
zh: 这其中是有勇气的，即使它同时也有助于品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for listening.
zh: 感谢收听。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey listeners, Bob here.
zh: 嗨，各位听众，我是 Bob。

zh: 如果你们只在 Masters of Scale 上收听 Rapid Response，那你们可能错过了节目的一半，因为每周五我们会在 Rapid Response 频道独家发布第二期 Rapid Response。

zh: 嘉宾和话题同样引人入胜、切合时宜，从福特 CEO 到 NASA 局长，再到《穿普拉达的女王》带给我们的启示。

zh: 找到它只需要大约 10 秒钟。

zh: 只要在你收听播客的任何平台搜索 Rapid Response，然后点击关注，确保你不错过任何一集。

en: I hope to see you there.
zh: 希望在那里见到你们。

zh: Rapid Response 是 Wait What 的原创节目。

zh: 我们的执行制片人是 Eve Trow。

zh: 助理制片人是 Mashumaku Tonina。
